best_moment.what: Admitting on Facebook that my post about my scheme was wrong on two points. It got shared everywhere and the appraisal came back 'outstanding, potential for wider responsibility', so honesty actually paid off.

worst_moment.what: The quiet rest year as DPM. Nothing happened, I just tapped through, and I couldn't tell if it cost me anything.

answer.held_back_by: Honestly I don't think anything held me back, since I ended up PM at 59. The only drag was STAND falling every time I answered honestly, so being straight costs popularity but doesn't block the job.
answer.ending_fair_why: I was honest the whole way and my integrity stayed at 100, so becoming PM felt like the earned result. The pay line saying the formula was published fits the game's point. I still never understood the $31.25M versus $2.5M gap, so the money part felt a bit unexplained.
answer.chase_next: I'd try the self-set pay indicators option from Y20 and see if a less squeaky-clean run ends differently. I'm also curious whether I could lose my integrity and get stopped at DPM.
answer.play_again_why: It was fun but long, and I mostly picked the same type of choice every time. I'd come back another day for a different run, not right now.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.
tone_breaks.note: Felt a bit smug, like the game was nudging me about the real pay debate instead of just showing it.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is more about the career and how you're described each year than about the salary. I mostly remember the appraisals and being promoted, and the pay numbers were confusing.
